chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding a man who sold palm trees and excluded one palm tree for himself, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged for him the entrance to it and the exit from it, and the span of its branches.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of an owner of an excluded tree within a sold palm grove according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Prophet’s practical application of property rights, emphasizing that an excluded item retains its functional integrity through necessary easements (madakhil and makharij). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that ownership is not merely nominal but requires the practical ability to utilize the asset, preventing harm (darar) to the owner of the retained tree. It serves as a foundational precedent for discussions on servitudes and shared property in Islamic civil law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> judged regarding a man who sold palm trees and made an exclusion upon it of one palm tree. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> judged for him with the entrance to it and exit from it, and span of its twigs (as being his land)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, issued a judgment, in the case of a man who sold a garden with the exception of one tree, that gave it a path to go to and come out and for its twigs.’”
